newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- T-bond traders sell out-of-money calls.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- T-bond traders sell out-of-money calls.

text.p: Implied volatilities for Treasury bond options edged slightly lower Thursday, with August dipping below 8.0 percent, as the underlying futures traded around unchanged late in the session.

Traders said sizable selling of out-of-the-money December bond calls was a feature in an otherwise quiet session. A U.S. commercial firm sold 5,000 December 120-00 calls outright, possibly to liquidate a previously set position, and a trading firm sold 2,000 of the same calls covered at 111-30 in futures.
Activity is shifting into August, which becomes the front month contract after July options cease trading Friday, floor brokers said.

Traders said the concentration of open interest in the July 112-00 calls was keeping September futures from straying too far from the strike. Futures have a tendency to gravitate toward the nearest strike as the options approach expiration.
September futures were up 2/32 at 112-07 near the close.
August implied volatility was pegged at about 7.95 percent late in the session, down 0.1 point from late Wednesday, and September was around 8.20 percent, also down 0.1 point.

Eurodollar volatility rose 0.1 point to 10.0 percent in December. A Eurodollar broker said options trading continued to be negatively slanted despite the recent uptrend in futures prices, suggesting investors are either protecting long futures positions or are anticipating an eventual Federal Reserve rate tightening.
Traders continued to acquire puts and put spreads in September and December, the broker said.
The trend of selling front-end volatility also continued, with selling of straddles concentrated in December and short-dated July midcurve options, he said.
